note: Hand-kept inputs for the Deep South border map (tools/build_deepsouth_border.mjs). Crossings: official checkpoints on the Thailand–Malaysia border, positions approximate. Special-law areas: which districts the Thai government says are under each special security law; government statements are claims, shown with their sources.
districts_note: District outlines: data/places/deepsouth-areas.json (geoBoundaries THA ADM2, CC BY 3.0 IGO).

measure_levels.decree: Emergency Decree on Public Administration in Emergency Situations (2005): the strongest of the three; detention without charge for a limited time and immunity for officials.
measure_levels.isa: Internal Security Act (2008), section 15: ISOC leads security; used where the Thai government says things have improved, in place of the decree.
measure_levels.martial: Martial Law Act (1914): not shown, because no current source confirming its districts was found.

crossings.name: Wang Prachan – Wang Kelian
crossings.why: Small road checkpoint in the hills of the Satun–Perlis border; the 2015 trafficking camps were found on the ridges near Wang Kelian.

crossings.name: Padang Besar (road and railway)
crossings.why: Road and the only working cross-border railway (Hat Yai–Padang Besar–Butterworth); busy trade and smuggling point.

crossings.name: Sadao (Dan Nok) – Bukit Kayu Hitam
crossings.why: Main road crossing (AH2 / North–South Expressway) and the largest trade crossing; customs and smuggling seizures are reported here often.

crossings.name: Ban Prakop – Durian Burung
crossings.why: Minor road checkpoint in Na Thawi, one of Songkhla's four special-security districts.

crossings.name: Betong – Pengkalan Hulu
crossings.why: Southernmost Thai road crossing; Betong town sits in a pocket of hills reached from Yala by Route 410.

crossings.name: Buketa – Bukit Bunga
crossings.why: Bridge over the upper Kolok river in Waeng district, close to the Hala-Bala forest.

crossings.name: Sungai Kolok – Rantau Panjang (road and railway bridge)
crossings.why: Busiest Narathiwat crossing; the river either side is lined with informal jetties used for smuggling (Malaysia reported closing 134 illegal jetties).

crossings.name: Tak Bai (Ta Ba) – Pengkalan Kubor (vehicle ferry)
crossings.why: Vehicle ferry across the Kolok river mouth; Tak Bai district is one of the most violent along the border.

crossings.name: Satun (Tammalang pier) – Perlis and Langkawi
crossings.why: Sea crossing by passenger boat from Satun to Perlis and Langkawi.

measures.name: Emergency Decree (serious emergency), 86th extension
measures.note: Cabinet extended it for 3 months, 20 Oct 2026 to 19 Jan 2027: all of Narathiwat except Yi-ngo, Waeng and Sukhirin; Pattani except Yaring, Panare, Mayo, Mai Kaen, Thung Yang Daeng, Kapho and Mae Lan; Yala except Betong, Yaha, Raman, Kabang and Krong Pinang. Su-ngai Kolok has been back under the decree since 20 Apr 2026. Government statement, a claim.

measures.name: Internal Security Act area, section 15
measures.note: Cabinet extended it for 1 year, 1 Oct 2026 to 30 Sep 2027 (22nd extension): Narathiwat 3 districts, Pattani 7, Yala 5 and Songkhla 4 (Na Thawi, Chana, Thepha, Saba Yoi). Su-ngai Kolok was taken out on 11 Apr 2026, leaving 19. Government statement, a claim.
